$comment: Why each tenant-bypass or raw-SQL site on the request path is safe. Completeness is the generator's job — it scans app/, lib/ and workers/ and renders every site it finds. This file is the half a scan cannot produce: the judgement. A site with no entry here renders as UNREVIEWED and turns the generator red, which is how a new bypass is stopped from being added quietly. Keyed by repository-relative path; one entry covers every site in that file.
$reviewedAgainst: 9b2b44c9f0987139e2f48ee21b14ec36e10690a8 plus the TEL-P0-013 fixes on this branch

rationales.app/api/ai/attention/route.ts: Session tenant from `requireAuth`. The scope wraps `getWhatNeedsAttention`, which filters every query in `lib/ai/engine/attention-engine.ts` by `tenantId` explicitly — overdue leads, unassigned leads and paused mailboxes all carry it.
rationales.app/api/ai/daily-briefing/route.ts: Session tenant from `requireAuth`. All three reads inside the scope — `task.findMany`, `lead.findMany`, `activity.findMany` — name `tenantId` in their `where` explicitly.
rationales.app/api/ai/nba/route.ts: Session tenant from `requireAuth`. The scope wraps `calculateNextBestAction`, which reads `lead.findFirst({ where: { id: leadId, tenantId } })` — the id is paired with the tenant, so a foreign id resolves to nothing.
rationales.app/api/cron/email-health/route.ts: System context (`tenantId: 'system'`), and deliberately cross-tenant: the job computes email health across every tenant. Reachable only with the `CRON_SECRET` bearer token, never from a user session.
rationales.app/api/cron/inbox-sync/route.ts: System context, deliberately cross-tenant: it sweeps active mailboxes across tenants to enqueue per-account sync jobs. `CRON_SECRET` bearer token only.
rationales.app/api/cron/maintenance/route.ts: System context, deliberately cross-tenant: it iterates tenants to schedule per-tenant maintenance. `CRON_SECRET` bearer token only.
rationales.app/api/cron/sequence-engine/route.ts: System context, deliberately cross-tenant: it scans due sequence steps for every tenant and processes each within its own tenant boundary. Task claims use a conditional `updateMany` on `id + status + lockedAt`, so two runners cannot both take a task. `CRON_SECRET` bearer token only.
rationales.app/api/leads/recalculate-scores/route.t: Session tenant from the verified `SessionUser`. The `lead.update` calls inside the scope address ids drawn from a preceding tenant-scoped read, so no caller-supplied id reaches the database.
rationales.app/api/unsubscribe/route.ts: Public by necessity — an unsubscribe link is followed without a session. The tenant is not taken from the request but recovered from an HMAC-verified token that binds `tenantId`, `email` and `leadId`; a forged or edited token fails verification before any query runs.
rationales.lib/auth.ts: Runs before a tenant is known, which is the reason the bypass exists. API keys are resolved by unique `keyHash` and users by the id inside an already-verified token; both are identity lookups whose whole purpose is to establish the tenant that later queries are scoped by.
rationales.lib/bullmq/enqueue.ts: Scoped to the payload's own `tenantId`, not to 'system'. The bypass exists so the `JobRun` mirror row can be written with the tenant stamped on it.
rationales.lib/bullmq/ensureJob.ts: Idempotent job creation. The `jobRun.findUnique({ where: { dedupeKey } })` lookup runs before the tenant is known — a dedupe key is global by construction, because its job is to notice a duplicate whoever enqueued it. The row it finds carries its own `tenantId`, which scopes everything after.
rationales.lib/bullmq/rescheduleSequenceTask.ts: Scoped to `input.tenantId`. The `jobRun` lookup by `dedupeKey` is the same pre-tenant identity lookup as `ensureJob`.
rationales.lib/bullmq/workerUtils.ts: Scoped to the tenant declared on the job payload. `jobRun.update` calls address the row by its own id, obtained from the job being executed.
rationales.lib/prisma.ts: The extension itself — this is the file that implements tenant scoping, so it necessarily names the flag it honours and runs the `set_config` statements that carry tenant context into the database. Its own `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` calls are the GUC statements and the maintenance sweep, not data access.
rationales.lib/workflows/importInline.ts: Scoped to `payload.tenantId`. The inline fallback runs when Redis is unavailable; its `importRow.count` calls are filtered by `batchId`, which belongs to the batch being imported.
rationales.lib/client-reports/shareLinks.ts: A public share link is followed without a session, so the tenant cannot come from one. It is recovered by looking up an unguessable 32-byte token by hash, reading only `tenantId` off the row, and scoping every subsequent read to it. `createShareLink` derives a tenant from the report only when its caller omits one; the sole caller passes `user.tenantId` from a verified session, and that route has no bypass scope of its own.
rationales.lib/db/adminClient.mjs: A deliberately unextended client for operator and test tooling that must reach across tenants — seeding, integrity checks, fixtures. Not imported by any request-path module.
rationales.app/api/admin/worker-health/route.ts: `SELECT 1` liveness probe. Touches no tenant-owned table.
rationales.app/api/health/route.ts: `SELECT 1` liveness probe. Touches no tenant-owned table, and the file says so in a comment for the same reason it appears here.
rationales.app/api/booking-links/route.ts: Raw SQL is a transaction-scoped advisory lock, taken so that clearing the previous default and setting the new one cannot interleave with a concurrent request. It reads no rows.
rationales.app/api/booking-links/[id]/route.ts: Same advisory lock as the collection route, for the same read-decide-write on the default flag.
rationales.lib/ai/budget.ts: Every statement goes through `withTenantRaw`, which sets `app.current_tenant_id` on the connection the statement runs on, except the sweep of expired reservations and the test-only truncations, which are `withBypassRaw` and cross-tenant on purpose — an expiry sweep cannot name one tenant.
rationales.lib/db/migrationStatus.ts: Reads `_prisma_migrations`, a schema table with no tenant column and no tenant data.
rationales.lib/leadgen/qualification.ts: Window-function aggregations for pool qualification, all routed through `withTenantRaw` and additionally naming `tenantId` in the WHERE clause.
rationales.lib/research/cache.ts: Cache updates through `withTenantRaw`, so the statement carries tenant context on its own connection.
rationales.lib/search/accentSearch.ts: Accent-insensitive search through `withTenantRaw`, with `tenantId` also named explicitly in the WHERE clause.
rationales.workers/email.ts: An atomic compare-and-set on `EmailAccount.sentTodayCount`, routed through `withTenantRaw` and addressing a single row by id. Raw SQL rather than a read-modify-write so two workers cannot both spend the last send of a quota.
rationales.workers/healthcheck.ts: `SELECT 1` liveness probe. Touches no tenant-owned table.
